subject: spanish

truths: “Me llevo bien con mis padres” means “I get on well with my parents”.
“Soy hijo único” means “I am an only child”.

rounds.lie: “Mi hermana es aburrida” means “My sister is bored”.
rounds.truth: “Mi hermana es aburrida” means “My sister is boring”.
truths: “Es muy trabajador” means “He is very hard-working”.

rounds.why: “Aprobado” is a pass (“aprobar” = to pass). “A fail” is “un suspenso” (“suspender” = to fail).

rounds.lie: “Tengo que repasar” means “I want to rest”.
rounds.why: “Repasar” = to revise and “tengo que” = I have to. “I want to rest” would be “quiero descansar”.
rounds.truth: “Tengo que repasar” means “I have to revise”.
truths: “Quiero ser enfermero” means “I want to be a nurse”.
“Hago mis deberes” means “I do my homework”.

rounds.why: Another false friend — “constipado” means “to have a cold”. “Constipated” is “estreñido”.
truths: “Llevo una vida sana” means “I lead a healthy life”.
“Evito la comida basura” means “I avoid junk food”.

rounds.lie: “Nos llevamos mal” means “We get on well”.
rounds.why: “Llevarse mal” = to get on badly. “We get on well” is “nos llevamos bien”.
rounds.truth: “Nos llevamos mal” means “We get on badly”.
truths: “Me apoya siempre” means “He/she always supports me”.

rounds.lie: “Estoy en paro” means “I am on a break”.
rounds.why: “Estar en paro” means “to be unemployed”. “On a break” would be “en un descanso”.
truths: “Trabajo a tiempo parcial” means “I work part-time”.

rounds.lie: The ending “simpáticas” describes a group of boys.
rounds.why: The “-as” ending is feminine plural, so it describes girls/women. A group of boys would be “simpáticos”.
rounds.truth: The ending “simpáticas” describes a group of girls/women.
